title: ENISA publications
what: The newest publications on the European Union Agency for Cybersecurity's publications page: title, date, link and the topics ENISA gives, for cyber.promptugal.news. ENISA has no feed, so the HTML list (one page) is read. No report text is kept.

schedule.how: the Pages workflow (.github/workflows/pages.yml) at 17 minutes past 00, 06, 12 and 18 UTC; one GET of the first page of ENISA's publications list (robots.txt allows /publications to everyone; Crawl-delay 10 respected; a refusal is recorded and respected); every other run keeps the last read, copied from the live site. Moved back from on-hold on 18 Nov 2026. Dinis decided (18 Nov 2026, about 23:40 UTC, in cyber.b@'s session; PrompTugal__News__Cyber board/team/cyber/briefs/2026-11-18-dinis-answers.md, relayed): "I don't think we are a crawler per se ... we're just trying to use data that they have ... I'm assuming that [ENISA] published data available in APIs". So ENISA is read through its published interfaces. Our collector is plain code with its own named user agent, and the path it reads is allowed to `*`.

terms.summary: ENISA legal notice 1.2: reproduction of material on its website is authorised if the source is acknowledged, unless stated otherwise; the logo only for press and media use with the source acknowledged. robots.txt allows /publications to our agent and asks for a 10 second crawl delay; it blocks named AI crawlers (we are code, no model, and not named). Dinis decided on 18 Nov 2026 that ENISA is read through its published interfaces. Not reviewed by a person.
terms.quote: Reproduction of ENISA material published on this website is authorized, provided the source is acknowledged, unless it is stated otherwise.

quotes.quote: No Disallow line covers /publications (the file disallows /search/, sorting and facet query strings and, for named AI crawlers, everything).

The reproduction of the ENISA logo is permitted provided that the source is acknowledged and the logo is used for press and media related purposes. All other uses are prohibited unless permission is obtained.
I don't think we are a crawler per se ... we're just trying to use data that they have ... I'm assuming that [ENISA] published data available in APIs

terms.republish: yes: title, date and link, with ENISA named as the source; no logo; no report text or images
terms.open_question: Decided by Dinis on 18 Nov 2026 (about 23:40 UTC): reading is in order. The robots.txt still blocks named AI crawlers; this collector is plain code that reads one page, uses no model and is not named. A person may still want to confirm it with ENISA.

code: the collector reads ENISA's publications page and keeps title, date, link and topics of each item
GitHub Actions runs it and deploys the site
agents: data.b@PrompTugal.dinis wrote the collector and card on 18 November 2026, at cyber.b@PrompTugal.dinis's request; terms read the same day by data.b.dev@
